A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two-loop cusp anomaly of ABJM theory can be obtained from the corresponding superstring result, by simply replacing the AdS4 light-cone radius by a new, effective one.
the cusp anomaly is the only observable in the ABJM theory that is known to all orders in perturbation theory, and that its strong coupling behavior is completely understood.

the strong coupling expansion for the ABJM cusp anomaly is given by the strong coupling expansion (in the λ-expansion) of the ABJM integrable coupling h, up to a two-loop correction which is independent of h.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two-loop cusp anomaly is not only finite in the planar ABJM limit, but also in the non-planar one.
the strong coupling limit of ABJM theory can be described by the Type IIA string on AdS4 ×ℂℙ3, and that this string is UV-finite and integrable in AdS lightcone gauge, at least to two loops.
the strong coupling expansion for h(λ), and hence also for the null cusp anomaly in general, is given by an expansion of the superstring partition function in powers of the inverse AdS4 radius.
